node.title: Reformulation: descent-tree size = closed-set count of the sparse-support lattice
node.statement: The naive descent tree is binary (2^depth danger), but tree nodes correspond to CLOSED SETS of the lattice generated by sparse-word supports (unions/closures = subflats + residual domains), with chain length <= dim P + deg drop. Tree size <= lattice size — the accounting identity that makes polynomial termination plausible at all, and the object the family bounds must count.
node.notes: PACKET WRITTEN (wave 1, verifier 31/31): batch/memoized form proved; the binary form carries a (1 + W_max) factor — both defuse 2^depth. CAVEATS recorded: conventions need reconciling with in-flight QF.6/QF.7 at integration; the identity RELOCATES the polynomial question to family-specific closed-set counting (as the E17 counterexample independently showed). | Positive residue from X-2: FIXED-d closed-set bound n^{O(d)} (trace-matroid rank argument) — every fixed dimension now has polynomial accounting; uniformity in d is impossible without the dihedral ledger. | FLIP on replay (Codex wave 4): PROVABLE -> PROVED.
